Katie Hobbs

Democratic candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Arizona · Incumbent

Governor of Arizona

Katie Hobbs is the Democratic Governor of Arizona and has held the office since January 2023. Before that she was Arizona Secretary of State and served in the state legislature. She won the 2026 Democratic nomination without an opponent and is running for a second term with former Mesa Mayor John Giles as her running mate.

Where Hobbs stands

Medicaid and health care
Opposes federal Medicaid cuts and says Arizona cannot absorb them. She rejected state GOP budget proposals that would have cut Medicaid.
School vouchers (ESAs)
Supports adding oversight and accountability to the Empowerment Scholarship Account program, including a way to claw back unused funds. She calls the current program a "billion-dollar boondoggle."
Border security and immigration
Says border security has been a focus since her first day in office. Started Operation Desert Guardian, a multi-agency effort against cartel activity, and says she works with the federal government on border security.
Water / Colorado River
Arizona, under her administration, joined Nevada's lawsuit against the U.S. Interior Department to block federal cuts to Lower Basin Colorado River water supplies.
Taxes and cost of living
Her campaign says she will work across party lines to cut taxes, erase medical debt for nearly 700,000 people, secure the border and protect water.
Food assistance (SNAP)
Criticized delays in federal SNAP benefits during the 2025 shutdown, saying nearly 900,000 Arizonans rely on the program. She considered declaring a state of emergency.
Proposition 144
Opposes Proposition 144 on the 2026 ballot.
Debates
Chose not to debate Andy Biggs. Her campaign says face-to-face engagement with Arizonans works better than a debate stage.

Background

  • Governor of Arizona, 2023–present
  • Arizona Secretary of State, 2019–2023
  • Arizona Senate Minority Leader, 2015–2019
  • Arizona State Senator, District 24, 2013–2019

  • Born in Phoenix, Arizona, 1969
